newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end pit trading barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end pit trading barely mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended quiet pit trading barely mixed as the market hunkered down before Friday's U.S. wholesale inflation and retail sales reports.
Most currencies nosed up to day's highs late, supported by the downward extension in December U.S. Treasury bond futures as that contract probed below key support levels.

Traders linked the move down in U.S. Treasuries to technicals and nervousness among longs that September's U.S. producer price index and retail sales figures could show more economic strength than originally forecast.
PPI on average was forecast rising 0.3 percent and gaining 0.2 percent in the core rate, both of which would fit neatly into the market's perception that inflation remains tame.
Retail sales were expected to rise 0.2 percent overall and increase 0.3 percent excluding automobiles.

"They're kind of trying to second-guess that PPI and retail sales might be a little out of line," said a floor analyst. "Short-term, it's (dollar) been up for two weeks but its frustrated traders" due to the lack of followthrough.
Most currencies continued to lack drive to bulge out the familiar price ranges that had hemmed in the market all week.
"We're stuck in this range," said another floor broker. "I'd like for the dollar to move to the upside but until then...there's no interest."
After an early bid dried up, the Canadian dollar briefly probed lower but respected support and edged back up late.
"It was bid early but it back off really good," said a another floor broker of the Canadian dollar, which for a while on Thursday moved in tandem with the buoyant yen.
"It normally goes inverse to yen and today they were going parallel," added the broker. "So I was looking to sell Canada but then it held."
The December Canadian dollar held support near $0.7416 and stayed perched above a double-bottom at the $0.7405 level.

The contract, also boosted on Thursday by optimism about the Canadian budget situation, rose as high as $0.7430, key resistance and the highest level the December futures had visited since October 11, 1995.
The Canadian dollar rose on finance minister Paul Martin's budget speech that analysts said proved constructive and could presage another Canadian rate cut.
Some expected no Canadian rate action, however, until after Friday's August Canadian employment report.

December yen rose $0.000034 to $0.009075, marks ended flat at $0.6570, Swiss francs rose $0.0025 to $0.8057, Sterling firmed $0.0012 to $1.5652, Canadian dollar added $0.0015 to $0.7427, Australian dollar eased $0.0004 to $0.7881, and the Mexican peso fell $0.000350 to $0.126500. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
